name: Ancient Royal Tombs of Lapaha
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See + tourism board name it; open 24/7 with information signs; the langi are the Tongatapu archaeological draw.
objection: Same ground as the Muʻa village entry; if both are listed they are near-duplicates (opened Wikivoyage Tongatapu).

name: Mapu 'a Vaea
reason: Rules 1-3: two counted sources; free 24/7 blowholes, a named natural sight on the west-coast route.
objection: Best only at high tide and with surf; a short stop.

name: Hufangalupe
reason: Rules 1-3: two counted sources; Wikivoyage calls it one of the most beautiful nature sights on the island; walk over the bridge.
objection: Short visit; remote south-east coast.

name: Royal Palace
reason: Rule 2: grounds closed, exterior only (Wikivoyage: no admission).
objection: A famous landmark guides name, but nothing to do beyond looking over the fence.

name: Talamahu Market
reason: Rules 1-4: two counted sources; daily market hall with handicrafts upstairs, so not a weekly market.
objection: Mostly a local produce market; low page views.

name: Tonga National Museum
reason: Rule 2 pass (open Mon-Fri, collection incl. Tuʻi Malila tortoise) but one counted source and a small museum.
objection: For: only national museum, capital. Against: one source, short visit, opening reliability uncertain.

name: Tukuʻaho Memorial Museum
reason: Rule 2: open by appointment only, small, one source.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it free with royal artefacts, but a visitor cannot just arrive.

name: Captain Cook Landing Site
reason: Rule 3: guidebook-named historic landmark, free, but probably a monument/plaque at a roadside; one source.
objection: For: Wikivoyage names it, Cook history. Against: minor marker, 10-minute stop.

name: Abel Tasman Landing Site
reason: Rule 3: one source, remote end of Hihifo Rd; likely a marker only.
objection: For: first European landing in Tonga. Against: minor memorial, nothing to do, remote.

name: Haʻatafu Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: two counted sources; beach with snorkelling and surf, second-tier stop that guides recommend.
objection: Resort-fronted; reaching it needs transport.

name: Matatahi 'Anahulu Beach
reason: Rule 3: near-duplicate of Anahulu Caves, a walk away, one source.
objection: A free beach is a legitimate stop, but it is the cave's neighbour with little on it.

name: Anahulu Caves
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage lists guided tours with a swim in the pools; an activity of 30+ minutes.
objection: One counted source; operator reliability unverified.

name: Niutao Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: one source, small beach with little on site.
objection: Free and open; but no draw.

name: Pangaimotu Island
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Do + tourism board; island day trip with wreck snorkel, restaurant. The island is the spot, not the boat.
objection: Resort island, boat needed.

name: Fafa Island
reason: Rule 1: one source mentions it only as a resort accommodation listing; day trip by ferry plausible.
objection: For: island day trip with beach. Against: Wikivoyage only lists the resort, day access unverified.

name: ʻAtata Island
reason: Rule 1: one source; resort island day trip/stay; no visitor source opened describing the visit.
objection: For: island with resort. Against: resort-only, one source.

name: Flying Fox Reserve
reason: Rule 1-2: Lonely Planet 'Flying Foxes' (Around Tongatapu) plus Tonga Pocket Guide name it; free roadside wildlife viewing at Kolovai, a regular stop on west-coast tours (opened web search results).
objection: Not an official reserve, ~30 min roadside stop; best at dusk.

name: Hule Fortress
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source found.
objection: Wikipedia-only archaeological earthwork.

name: Nukuleka
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source found.
objection: Archaeologically important but nothing for visitors.

name: Malaʻe Kula
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says the royal tomb is the most popular site to visit; one source; cemetery visitors view from outside.
objection: For: named sight in capital. Against: cemetery etiquette, one source, essentially exterior.

name: Centenary Church
reason: Rule 2 church test: Wikivoyage names only the royal Easter attendance; no interior or tour; seen from outside.
objection: Famous royal church; Sunday services draw visitors, but that is an event.

name: Nukuʻalofa Cathedral
reason: Rule 2: ruin, entry not permitted.
objection: Striking facade is visible, but a damaged exterior only.

name: Basilica of St Anthony of Padua
reason: Church test: Wikivoyage singles out its unusual pagoda-like Polynesian architecture; free; one source.
objection: For: notable architecture a guide singles out. Against: one source, short stop.

name: St Mary's Cathedral
reason: Church test: only generic architecture remark, one source, no interior or tour.
objection: Wikivoyage calls it architecturally interesting; thin.

name: Ancient Tonga
reason: Rule 4: a Friday buffet and show, an event/operator rather than a place.
objection: Two counted sources, but it is a recurring show.

name: Oholei Beach Dinner and Show
reason: Rule 4 tension: a dinner show in Hina cave, booked ahead; the cave venue is permanent but visits are the show; no coordinates.
objection: For: two counted sources, a well-known Tongan cultural venue. Against: weekly show event, dinner not a place; needs coordinates.
